test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 7 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A train is travelling 50% faster than a bus. Both start from Karnal at the same time and reach Panipat, which is 75 km from Karnal at the same time. On the way however, the train stopped at a station for about 12.5 minutes. The speed of the bus is:
solution:
**Given:**

Train is travelling 50% faster than a bus

Distance between Karnal and Panipat = 75 km

Time = 12.5 min

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the bus be x km/h

Then,

Speed of the train = (150/100)x = (3/2)x km/h

According to the question

⇒ 75/x – 75/(3/2)x = (125/10 × 60)

⇒ 75/x – 50/x = 5/24

⇒ 25/x = 5/24

⇒ x = (25 × 24)/5

⇒ x = 120 km/h

**∴ The speed of the bus is 120 km/h.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** The speed of the bus = 2x km/hr

then, the speed of train = 150% of 2x = 3x km/hr

let time taken by train and bus each = y hours

and

Distance = Speed × time

⇒ 3x × y = 2x × (y + 12.5/60)

⇒ 3xy = 2xy + (5/12)x

⇒ y = 5/12 hours

and we know, the distance is 75 km.

So, 3xy = 75

⇒ 3x × (5/12) = 75

⇒ x = 60 km/hr

So,

**The speed of Bus = 2x = 2 × 60 = 120 km/hr **
